meta.source: Hot Water Math installation cost ranges, anchored to the U.S. Department of Energy's 2024 consumer water heater rules (installation costs built from RSMeans) and Home Depot listing prices, and checked against published industry ranges
meta.notes: No public source publishes plumber labor by job type in a form we can reprint: DOE builds its installation costs from paid RSMeans data and publishes averages only. So these low / typical / high ranges are our own estimate, written down with the references each one leans on. Where DOE gives a figure, the typical value is that figure (or sits next to it); where DOE gives a range, low and high come from it. Industry cost guides are used only as a sanity check, never as the source of a number. Labor and extras are multiplied by the state price factor (regional-cost-index.json); equipment is not. Review every three months.

doe-storage-2024.publisher: U.S. Department of Energy, Federal Register
doe-storage-2024.title: Energy conservation standards for consumer water heaters, final rule (89 FR 37778, May 6, 2024)
quotes: Installation cost covers all labor, overhead, and material costs associated with the replacement of an existing water heater ... delivery of the new water heater, removal of the existing water heater, and any applicable permit fees.
Table V.2: gas-fired storage (20-55 gal), baseline average installed cost $1,432 (2022$).
Table V.8: electric storage (20-55 gal), baseline (electric resistance) $902; efficiency level 1 (heat pump) $1,855 (2022$).
Panel upgrade costs are significant and can be approximately $750--$2,000 to upgrade to a 200-amp electrical panel.
The installation of a new 240-volt circuit by a qualified electrician will be at least several hundred dollars.
Heat pump water heaters: a distribution of installation cost adders that ranges from $0 to $4,000 in total for the most challenging installations, averaging $2,000.

doe-gas-tankless-2024.publisher: U.S. Department of Energy, Federal Register
doe-gas-tankless-2024.title: Energy conservation standards for consumer gas-fired instantaneous water heaters, final rule (89 FR 105188, December 26, 2024)
quotes: DOE estimated an average installation cost of $1,102 for non-condensing units and $1,025 for condensing units.
Table 8D.5.66 in the final rule TSD estimates permitting, removal, and disposal costs of $260.
Relocation costs in the case of electric storage water heaters could range up to $2,000.
Rinnai stated the Department's estimated venting costs of $499 for non-condensing ... and $263 for condensing gas-fired instantaneous water heater overstate the cost differential.
Table V.2: gas-fired instantaneous, baseline average installed cost $2,087 (2023$); first year's operating cost $303.

meta.note: Installing the new heater where the old one stood: disconnect and take out the old unit, set the new one, reconnect water, gas or power and the existing vent, fittings and connectors, fill and start up. Permit, haul-away and anything new (venting, gas line, circuit) are separate extras.

gas_tank.why: DOE's average installed cost for a standard gas tank ($1,432 in 2022 dollars, equipment included) leaves several hundred dollars for installation; industry guides give $150-$800 labor.

electric_tank.why: No vent or gas connection, so less work than gas; DOE's electric average ($902 installed, 2022 dollars) is its lowest of all types.

heat_pump.why: A heavier, taller unit plus a condensate drain. Extra work for tight spaces is a separate extra, as in DOE's analysis.

gas_tankless.why: DOE's average installation cost is $1,102 (non-condensing) and $1,025 (condensing), including about $260 for permit, removal and disposal, which we list separately; industry guides give $800-$1,500 labor.

electric_tankless.why: Wall mounting and wiring to existing circuits; new circuits or a panel upgrade are extras. DOE did not analyze electric tankless units.

permit.label: Permit, haul-away and disposal of the old unit
permit.why: Typical = DOE's $260 for permitting, removal and disposal; industry guides give $25-$300 for the permit and $100-$500 for removal.

expansionTank.label: Thermal expansion tank, parts and labor
expansionTank.why: The tank itself lists for $34-$67 at Home Depot; the rest is about an hour of labor and fittings.

codeItems.label: Code items: drain pan, seismic straps, relief valve piping
codeItems.why: A drain pan lists for about $12; strapping and drain work are mostly labor. Which items apply depends on your local code.

venting.label: New or changed venting
venting.why: DOE's earlier estimate was $499 for a non-condensing tankless vent and $263 for a condensing one; industry guides give $300-$1,000.

gasLine.label: Gas line upgrade or new gas line
gasLine.why: Industry guides give $275-$1,000; a tankless unit often needs a larger line than the tank it replaces.

circuit.label: New 240-volt circuit
circuit.why: DOE: "at least several hundred dollars"; industry guides give $300-$800 for electrical work.

panel.label: Electrical panel upgrade (to 200 amps)
panel.why: DOE's range is about $750-$2,000; typical is the middle of that range.

relocation.label: Moving the heater to a new spot
relocation.why: DOE says relocation can cost up to $2,000; new water, gas or power lines to the new spot are the main cost.

heatPumpSpace.label: Heat pump space work (louvered door, ducting, condensate pump)
heatPumpSpace.why: DOE's adders for the most challenging heat pump installs run $0-$4,000 and average $2,000.

replace.label: Replacing a heater of the same kind

fuelSwitch.label: Switching fuel (gas to electric or electric to gas)

toTankless.label: Replacing a tank with a tankless unit

maintenance.note: Yearly upkeep added to the running cost in the tankless vs tank tool (audit F-03, suggestion S-2). Priced as do-it-yourself work with the manufacturer steps; a plumber's service call costs more, and we found no listing we could reprint for it. Each line is perTimeUsd × timesPerYear, plus onceUsd spread over the unit's life, plus partUsd every everyYears.

tankless.label: Yearly descaling flush (vinegar, flush kit spread over the unit's life)
tankless.why: Rinnai: flush mineral deposits "at least once a year" with "4 gallons (15.1 liters) of undiluted white vinegar". Four 1-gallon jugs of 5% distilled white vinegar: $11.99 a case (WebstaurantStore). Pump, hoses and bucket: Rheem tankless flush kit RTG20124, $155.19 (Home Depot), bought once.

tank.label: Anode rod every 4 years (yearly tank flush with a garden hose: no parts)
tank.why: Rheem: "Flush the tank annually; replace the anode rod every 3-4 years" (we use 4, the longer end). Anode price: median of five standard magnesium or aluminum rods listed at Home Depot ($28.09 to $40.16; the powered rod is left out).

rinnai-flush.title: Flushing my Rinnai tankless water heater
quotes: It's important to flush those mineral deposits at least once a year.
Use 4 gallons (15.1 liters) of undiluted white vinegar to clean your tankless water heater.
